title: Incoming active slices in symmetric operadic families
statement:
Use symmetric operadic families, active simplices and their inert projections from [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], join slices of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], active concatenation from [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation], and categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $M^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^n$ be a small symmetric operadic family, $n\geq1$. Write $M_0^\otimes$ for its fiber at $0$. Let $\sigma:\Delta^r\to M^\otimes$ be an active simplex all of whose vertices have strictly positive $\Delta^n$-coordinate. Put $X=M_0^\otimes\times_{M^\otimes}M^\otimes_{/\sigma}$, and let $X_{\mathrm{act}}\subseteq X$ be the full subcategory of cones all of whose cross edges are active. The inclusion $X_{\mathrm{act}}\hookrightarrow X$ admits a left adjoint, given by the inert-active factorization of the incoming arrows. Write $J_b=M_0^\otimes\times_{M^\otimes}(M^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})_{/b}$ for an incoming active slice.
For any object $b$ of positive coordinate over $\langle s\rangle$, and chosen inert projections $b\to b_j$, inert-active factorization gives an equivalence
$$J_b\simeq\prod_{j=1}^s J_{b_j}.$$
Under this equivalence the source tuple and the canonical cone to $b$ identify coherently with the concatenation of the source tuples and canonical cones to $b_j$. These identifications persist after applying any inert-preserving family map to a symmetric infinity-operad, including all cocone composition homotopies. For $s=0$ the product is terminal and its tuple is empty.

September 18, 2017 edition inspected online. WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: The join-slice projection is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], and its pullback to $M_0^\otimes$ is a right fibration, so $X$ is a quasicategory. Restriction to the first vertex of $\sigma$ is a trivial Kan fibration by [lem-coef-initial-poset-slice-restriction], first in $M^\otimes$ and then in $M^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ with full coordinate-zero subcategory $(M_0^\otimes)_{\mathrm{act}}$. The lifting statement fixes prescribed source simplices, boundaries, and cone triangles; the right-fibration mapping-space description [lem-cbc-right-fibration-morphism-space] therefore applies to these coherent extensions. Between active cones the source pointed map is active, since its composite with an active map is active. Thus the second application describes precisely the full active-cone subcategory. Fullness of the parameter-zero subcategories follows because $[n]$ has only identity endomorphisms.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative factorization, block decomposition, and coherent cone identifications.

proof.text: For $C$ with source $x$, factor its first arrow by [lem-coef-symmetric-family-inert-active-orthogonality] through $x\to x_D$ in the zero fiber. By the first-vertex lifting of [lem-coef-initial-poset-slice-restriction], extend the factored arrow and its unit triangle to a cone $L(C)$ over $\sigma$. All its cross edges are active, since the first arrow and the edges of $\sigma$ are active. Orthogonality identifies the spaces of incoming-arrow triangles into every active cone, and [lem-cbc-right-fibration-morphism-space] identifies these with the full cone mapping spaces after the contractible first-vertex extensions. Hence $\operatorname{Map}_X(C,A)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{X_{\mathrm{act}}}(L(C),A)$ naturally in active $A$.

proof.text: For an active arrow $a:x\to b$, the fibers $D_j=\alpha^{-1}(j)$ and the inert lifts of the block projections give the coherent forward functor $P:J_b\to\prod_jJ_{b_j}$, including its action on triangles and higher simplices, by [lem-coef-symmetric-family-block-restriction].

proof.text: Given active arrows $a_j:x_j\to b_j$, the relative Segal homotopy-pullback square in [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] and active concatenation in [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation] assemble them into the active arrow and component triangles supplied by [lem-coef-symmetric-family-block-assembly]. This defines the inverse construction $Q$ without concatenating cross-parameter arrows.

proof.text: The slice right-fibration mapping formula [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], together with the coherent triangle clauses in the two block nodes, shows that $P$ and $Q$ act on all mapping spaces and higher simplices, including empty blocks.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative factorization, block decomposition, and coherent cone identifications.

proof.text: Check the two composites, including the source and cone comparisons. For a tuple $(a_j)$, the blocks of the active pointed map used to define $Q$ are its original input blocks. The projections of $\bigoplus_jx_j$ onto these blocks recover $x_j$ and $a_j$ by the inert cocartesian universal property in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. This gives $PQ\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Conversely, the blocks $\alpha^{-1}(j)$ of an active $a:x\to b$ exhaust its inputs. The fiber Segal axiom for the operad $M_0^\otimes$, as stated in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], reconstructs $x$ from those colors; the symmetric concatenation of [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation] gives the equivalence $\bigoplus_jx_j\simeq x$, allowing the permutation which puts the blocks consecutively. Under this equivalence, $a$ and the arrow constructed by $Q$ have the same output components $a_jp_j$. The relative Segal equivalence of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] identifies the arrows together with their component homotopies. Naturality of these mapping-space comparisons gives $QP\simeq\mathrm{id}$. The cone mapping formula in [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus], applied to the opposite quasicategory so that its left cones are the cocones used here, retains the specified composition paths, so these natural equivalences identify the whole canonical cone, as well as its source diagram. Their components are equivalences by the pointwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The quasi-inverse characterization in [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] now gives the categorical equivalence asserted in the statement.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative factorization, block decomposition, and coherent cone identifications.

proof.text: Let $F:M^\otimes\to E^\otimes$ be an inert-preserving family map. It preserves all base pointed maps, hence the blocks $D_j$ and activity; by the family-map definition [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] it sends each $p_j$ and each $b\to b_j$ to an inert edge. Consequently the image of the triangle defining $a_j$ is the factorization triangle for $F(a)$ through $F(p_j)$. Its identification with any chosen factorization in $E^\otimes$ is the contractible comparison specified by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. The restriction $F|_{M_0^\otimes}$ is a map of symmetric infinity-operads, so [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation] identifies $F(\bigoplus_jx_j)$ with $\bigoplus_jF(x_j)$ and preserves the symmetry, associativity and unit coherences used in step 7. Each output component of the image cone is $F(a_j)F(p_j)$, with its actual image composition homotopy. The output mapping-space Segal axiom in $E^\otimes$, stated in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], then identifies this image cone with the assembled output cones. Naturality in the ambient quasicategory of the join-cone comparison [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus], applied to opposite quasicategories as in step 7, ensures that these are identifications of diagrams and coherent cones in every simplicial degree. This proves the claimed compatibility after applying $F$; it does not assert that the induced functor from $J_b$ to the active slice in $E^\otimes$ is itself an equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative factorization, block decomposition, and coherent cone identifications.

proof.text: For $s=0$, an active pointed map $\langle k\rangle\to\langle0\rangle$ exists exactly when $k=0$. Thus every object of $J_b$ has the empty source tuple. The zero fiber of $M_0^\otimes$ is a terminal quasicategory up to equivalence by the fiber Segal axiom of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], and it is nonempty. The relative Segal square of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] at $b$ has a point in both product positions, so its left vertical map is an equivalence. In particular, for each empty-tuple source $x$ its homotopy fiber at the unique base map $(0,\langle0\rangle)\to(t,\langle0\rangle)$ is contractible; hence such incoming arrows exist. For any two such arrows, the space of source maps is contractible and the space of compatible triangles is contractible by [lem-cbc-right-fibration-morphism-space]. Therefore $J_b$ is equivalent to the point, as required for the empty product. The canonical cone still has its apex and the arrow from the empty source tuple; it is not an empty diagram. Its source tuple is the unit of [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation]. For $s=1$ the only block is the whole input tuple, so $P$ and $Q$ are the identity up to their specified unit coherences. A nullary arrow into a color has an empty block and is retained in steps 4-5, since no block was required nonempty. The proof of steps 1-3 also permits $D=\varnothing$, repeated positive coordinates of $\sigma$, and $r=0$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NI-470bda860 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's 9 steps, all 3 new nodes and every cited statement in full. HA Thm 3.1.2.3 step (1) is not archived (the report lists it as WANTED, proof_origin=agent), so I checked the steps against the cited nodes and the mathematics, not the printed page. Steps: (1) the initial-poset lemma applies in M and in M_act with fiber M_0 full in M; a morphism between active cones is active, since gamma eta active forces eta active. (2) i is the stationary inert edge in M_0. The right-fibration formula gives Map_X(C,A)=hofib_h, and the orthogonality square for i against the active edge a_A identifies it with hofib_a. (3) The dual pointwise-adjoint clause is stated in the cited node. Steps 4-6 cite the two block nodes; steps 7-9 are the earlier reviewed arguments renumbered, and I rechecked s=0: Segal with r=0 gives Map(x,b) a point. New nodes. Orthogonality is true: the cocartesian criterion and pasting reduce it to the base square. Its S part is trivial because the S-edge is an identity. Its Fin_* part is a strict pullback, since beta inert and gamma active force f to kill beta^-1(*). Edge cases D empty, beta=id and S=Delta^0 are fine. It does not duplicate lem-coef-symmetric-inert-active-orthogonality or lem-coef-operadic-inert-active-factorization, which concern a single operad. Block-restriction is true (it constructs the functor L composed with (b->b_j)_*) and asserts no equivalence. Block-assembly is true: the relative Segal fiber over (alpha,0->t) is a product of factors, each equivalent to Map(x_j,b_j) by cocartesianness of p_j, so the space is contractible. It does not assert QP=id. No node restates a clause of the item; there is no cycle and no SGA citation. proof_deps equals the union of uses, and every step is under 2000 characters. I accept both lem-cbc tool_uses as generic tools. No fixes.
